description: issue #332 (A2), closing the gap A1's reviewer flagged: A1 (#331) parses `explain`/`why`/`hint`/`debug` as ordinary zero-arity `Call`/`ParenCall` nodes with no static arity check, matching Turtle/Data precedent, so `(explain 1)` parses and checks clean. A2 rejects any nonzero-input parenthesized meta-command call AT RUNTIME with the stable `ol-too-many-inputs` diagnostic (spec/error-model.md) — reusing the same builder every other arity violation in the runtime uses — and emits no `tutor-output` event. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why only one report survives and it reads `stage: "semantic"`.
